summary: The Ghana Immigration Service's eVisa applicant guide distinguishes visa-free entry, which it lists for ECOWAS and AES nationals, from the Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) and the eVisa, and says to use the official eligibility checker before applying. Its ETA guide says the ETA regime applies to nationals of all African Union member states, all ECOWAS member states and countries holding a current bilateral visa waiver agreement with Ghana, and that there is no fee to apply. The eVisa costs USD 260 with standard processing, and the immigration officer sets the stay on entry, up to 60 days; Ghana's diplomatic missions abroad also issue visas.

tips.text: The Ghana Immigration Service's ETA Applicant Guide says the ETA regime applies to nationals of all African Union member states, all ECOWAS member states and countries holding a current bilateral visa waiver agreement with Ghana, and that the ETA is free.

The Ghana Immigration Service says to use the official eligibility checker before starting an application: its eVisa process distinguishes between visa-free entry, ETA eligibility and eVisa requirements, and eligibility depends on nationality, passport type and applicable government policy.

The Ghana Immigration Service tells eVisa travellers to carry the required yellow fever vaccination certificate or card. It says the certificate is required for entry and may be checked at the port of entry, and that travellers without it may be referred to airport health officials for the applicable health procedure, including vaccination where necessary.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Ghana?
faq.answer: It depends on your passport. The Ghana Immigration Service's eVisa applicant guide distinguishes visa-free entry, which it lists for ECOWAS and AES nationals, from the Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) and the eVisa, and says to use the official eligibility checker before applying. Its ETA guide says the ETA regime applies to nationals of all African Union member states, all ECOWAS member states and countries holding a current bilateral visa waiver agreement with Ghana, and that there is no fee to apply. The eVisa costs USD 260 with standard processing, and the immigration officer sets the stay on entry, up to 60 days; Ghana's diplomatic missions abroad also issue visas. The UK government says British citizens must have a visa to visit Ghana, and Canada's travel advice says a tourist visa is required for Canadians.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Ghana?
faq.answer: No official source we could read states in words whether US citizens need a visa; Ghana's eVisa portal gives the result for each nationality in its eligibility checker. For travellers who need one, the Ghana eVisa costs USD 260 with standard processing within 96 hours; Ghana currently issues single-entry eVisas only, valid for 90 days from the date of issue, and the immigration officer at the port of entry determines the stay, up to 60 days. The Embassy of Ghana in Washington lists USD 60 for a single-entry visa (USD 100 expedited).

faq.question: Is Ghana visa-free for African passport holders?
faq.answer: Ghana's eVisa applicant guide lists ECOWAS and AES nationals under visa-free entry, subject to applicable entry conditions. Its ETA Applicant Guide says the ETA regime applies to nationals of all African Union member states, all ECOWAS member states and countries holding a current bilateral visa waiver agreement with Ghana; the ETA is obtained before travelling to Ghana, there is no fee to apply, and the maximum permitted stay under it is 90 days from the date of entry.

faq.question: Can I get a visa on arrival in Ghana?
faq.answer: The Ghana Immigration Service says that where a person appears before an immigration officer without a visa, an Emergency Entry Visa (EEV) or Visa on Arrival may be granted, subject to conditions prescribed in the Regulations and to other conditions the officer may impose. Its fees table lists USD 200 for an EEV permit or emergency visa. The application is a letter addressed to the Comptroller-General of Immigration, with attached documents that include the bio data pages of the host and of the guest.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever vaccination for Ghana?
faq.answer: Yes. The Ghana Immigration Service says a valid yellow fever vaccination certificate or card is required for entry into Ghana and may be checked at the port of entry.

summary.text: Ghana's eVisa process distinguishes between visa-free entry, Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) eligibility and eVisa requirements. Eligibility depends on nationality, passport type and applicable government policy. Use the official eligibility checker before starting an application.

Visa-Free The traveller is eligible to enter Ghana without obtaining a visa, subject to applicable entry conditions. Check the current visa-free list and applicable passport category. See: ECOWAS & AES Nationals
The ETA regime applies to nationals of: All African Union (AU) member states. All ECOWAS member states. Countries holding a current bilateral visa waiver agreement with Ghana.
The ETA is not a visa — it is a free pre-travel security authorisation for eligible nationals. There is no fee to apply. The maximum permitted stay under the ETA is 90 days from the date of entry.
On entry, the immigration officer at the port of entry determines the permitted length of stay, up to a maximum of 60 days.
Visas issued in any of Ghana’s 56 Diplomatic Missions abroad cover single or multiple journeys for periods between six months to five years.

entryRequirements.proofOfFunds.text: Proof of sufficient funds, such as a bank statement or credit card statement covering the last 3 months.

entryRequirements.customs.currencyLimits.text: You must declare all hard currency, using the declaration form provided on arrival. You can bring in up to a maximum Ghanaian cedi equivalent of 10,000 US dollars.
Do not carry more than 10,000 dollars in value in any foreign currency. The Ghanaian authorities can confiscate the entire amount if you are carrying cash of this value or more.

countryFacts.safety.text: FCDO advises against all but essential travel to the Bawku Municipal area in the Upper East region of Ghana.
Several terrorist groups operate in neighbouring Burkina Faso near to Ghana’s northern border

countryFacts.bestTimeToVisit.text: The rainy season extends from March to November.
The harmattan, a burning, dusty and sand-filled wind, blows in from the Sahara from December to March. The harmattan can cause disruptions to travel.
